text.p: Loss-making Portuguese ship repairer Lisnave-Estaleiros Navais de Lisboa is bankrupt and all its shareholders will bear the loss from its reduction in capital, its president Jose de Mello said on Monday.
"The company is bankrupt," Mello told state television in an interview.
"There will be a reduction in the capital, and all the shareholders, big and small, will bear the loss," Mello said.
"We are not trying to save the company (via its restructuring). We are trying to create a completely new company," he added.
The company last month announced a drastic reduction in its capital to 3.6 billion escudos from 35.6 billion.
Lisnave has announced that it plans to set up a new operating company for the ship repair business which will absorb only part of the workforce currently on its books.
The remainder of the workers will become employees of a "human resources" company.
A recent rise in the shares of Lisnave was speculative, Mello said.
Trade in Lisnave shares was interrupted on Lisbon bourse earlier today.
